case_studies.title: Guntur Red Chilli JNPT Port Detention: Aflatoxin > 10 ppb Crisis
case_studies.trigger: Pre-shipment sampling by buyer nominated surveyor at JNPT CFS reported total Aflatoxin at 12.4 ppb, exceeding the EU statutory threshold of 10 ppb (B1 max 5 ppb).
case_studies.bottleneck: Shipping line issued detention notice; container moved to CFS holding bay incurring ₹7,500/day ground rent and ₹12,000/day reefer plug-in fees. Buyer threatened to cancel LC.
resolution_steps: 1. Invoked Spices Board of India Mandatory Export Quality Sampling protocol under Spices Board Act 1986.
2. Commissioned emergency re-test with Vimta Labs NABL Accredited laboratory TC-5012 using HPLC-FLD fluorescence method.
3. Result confirmed batch split: 80% was sub-5 ppb, but outer 20 bags absorbed moisture during monsoon road haulage from Guntur.
4. Executed on-dock de-stuffing, segregated contaminated bags, replaced with buffer inventory from cold storage in Navi Mumbai, and re-stuffed within 48 hours.
case_studies.statutory_defense: Spices Board Circular SEC/EXP/AFL/2023 & DGFT Notification No. 12/2015-2020: Proof of sorting and re-inspection certificate accepted for customs port clearance.
case_studies.financial_outcome: Demurrage capped at ₹39,000 (3 days). Saved ₹38.5L consignment from overseas border rejection and incineration penalty.

case_studies.title: Dubai Bank Letter of Credit Refusal: The 1-Day Bill of Lading Clash
case_studies.trigger: Issuing bank in Dubai rejected document presentation citing discrepancy: Bill of Lading showed Shipped on Board date 28-Aug, while LC stipulated Latest Shipment Date 27-Aug.
case_studies.bottleneck: Buyer attempted to exploit the rejection to demand a 15% discount before taking delivery, leaving exporter facing return freight of ₹6.5 Lakhs.
resolution_steps: 1. Intermediary / Exporter audited shipping line pre-carriage notes and Mates Receipt (MR) signed by port captain.
2. Discovered cargo was physically received into port customs custody and loaded on feeder vessel on 26-Aug; the ocean carrier mistakenly stamped the mother vessel sail date.
3. Requested ocean line to issue statutory Carrier Certificate confirming cargo was in charge of carrier within LC shipment window.
4. Dispatched formal ICC UCP 600 Article 14(b) & Article 16 notice through exporter bank (State Bank of India Overseas Branch), demanding payment honor within 5 banking days.
case_studies.statutory_defense: ICC Banking Commission Opinion R.350 & UCP 600 Article 14(a): Banks must examine documents on their face; carrier on-board notation dated within window supersedes automated vessel sail timestamps.
case_studies.financial_outcome: Issuing bank backed down and remitted 100% of $760,000 USD on Day 4. Zero discount yielded.

case_studies.title: Moradabad Brass Artware: Structuring a ₹0-Capital 3% Commission Deal
case_studies.trigger: A boutique home decor retailer in Germany wanted direct artisan pricing on 2,500 brass planters, but small Moradabad workshops lacked IEC, export packaging, or English negotiation capacity.
case_studies.bottleneck: Artisans feared foreign fraud; buyer refused advance wire; broker lacked ₹42 Lakhs working capital to buy the inventory outright.
resolution_steps: 1. Broker executed tripartite Non-Circumvention Non-Disclosure Agreement (NCNDA) + Bank IMFPA with the Moradabad factory owner.

2. Structured deal with buyer opening an Irrevocable Transferable LC at Sight in favor of the factory merchant export partner, with 3% commission irrevocably wired to broker bank account upon presentation.
3. Supervised container stuffing at ICD Moradabad (CONCOR Railhead) to ensure export palletizing and barcode labeling.
4. Handed documentation package (Invoices, Packing List, Certificate of Origin) to CHA for ICEGATE filing.
case_studies.statutory_defense: Reserve Bank of India Master Direction No. 16/2015-16: Commission earnings repatriated in foreign currency through authorized banking channels are 100% exempt from GST under export-of-services Rule 6A.
case_studies.financial_outcome: Broker invested ₹0 capital. Earned ₹1,26,000 net commission wired directly upon shipment sailing.

case_studies.title: Tirupur Garments Drawback Freeze: Unlocking ₹4.2 Lakhs via PFMS Scrub
case_studies.trigger: Customs cleared shipment and vessel departed, but electronic Duty Drawback scroll status showed Stalled: SB002 PFMS Name Mismatch.
case_studies.bottleneck: Exporter registered name on GSTIN was ABC Texwear Private Limited, whereas bank account verified by PFMS was registered as ABC Texwear Pvt Ltd. Automated customs refund scroll rejected disbursal.
resolution_steps: 1. Diagnosed error code via ICEGATE Financial Services & Central Bank Verification ledger.
2. Generated ICICI Bank Authorized Dealer (AD) Code Verification Certificate certifying exact account entity identity.
3. Logged into ICEGATE portal -> Advisory Services -> Bank Account Management -> Initiated Single Rupee Test Credit.
4. Drafted and submitted statutory rectification letter under Section 149 of Customs Act 1962 to Assistant Commissioner (Drawback) at Chennai Seaport.
case_studies.statutory_defense: Customs Circular No. 33/2019-Customs: Automated re-validation mandated within 48 hours once bank validation certificate is verified by PFMS.
case_studies.financial_outcome: Scroll unlocked in 48 hours; ₹4,11,800 direct drawback cash credited to exporter bank account.
